hints.title: Sign Inversion Index Marking
hints.text: The array numbers range from one to n. Each element can act as an index into the array itself. How can sign negation flag visited values in place?

hints.title: Negative Marking Invariant
hints.text: Visiting index abs(val) minus one and negating the value reveals the duplicate when the target index already holds a negative number.

hints.title: Two Pass In Place Marking Procedure
hints.text: Traverse the array. For each number, examine the entry at index abs(n) minus one. If already negative, that absolute value is the duplicate; otherwise negate it. In a second pass, the single index holding a positive value corresponds to index plus one as the missing number.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sorting takes O(N log N) time, while hash sets allocate O(N) auxiliary space instead of constant space.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using sign marking directly in the array achieves O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should articulate in-place sign inversion or mathematical sum / sum-of-squares formulas to achieve O(1) auxiliary space.
